basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 14.' and it opens 'VERS. 14.-- Fac tibi arcam de lignis laevigatis. Ligna laevigata, fortia et insolubilia,'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 14.-- Fac tibi arcam de lignis laevigatis. Ligna laevigata, fortia et insolubilia, de quibus alia translatio dicit quadrata, ut arca nec ventorum vi | nec aquarum inundatione solveretur. Et bitumine facies intrinsecus et extrinsecus. Bitumen est ferventissimum et inviolatissimum gluten, cujus est virtus ut ligna ex eo linita nec vermibus exedi, nec solis ardore, vel ventorum flatibus, vel aquarum possint inundationibus dissolvi.
